title: Plant biology
summary: Plant tissues, how water and food are transported, plant hormones and reproduction
cards.0.p: The root anchors the plant in the soil and absorbs water and minerals. The root cap protects the tip of the root, and root hairs enlarge the absorbing surface. The stem holds the leaves up toward the light and transports substances.
cards.0.key: Root hairs are extensions of epidermal cells. A carrot stores food in its root.
cards.0.once.soru: Which organ is the potato tuber we eat?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: The eyes on a potato are buds, and buds are found on stems.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: A carrot is a root, but a potato tuber is an underground stem.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: A tuber is not a leaf. It is a stem that stores food.
cards.1.p: The waxy cuticle reduces water loss. The tightly packed palisade mesophyll carries out most of the photosynthesis. The loosely packed spongy mesophyll makes gas exchange easier. Stomata are mostly on the underside of the leaf.
cards.1.key: The veins in a leaf are vascular bundles. Epidermal cells usually have no chloroplasts, but guard cells do.
cards.1.etk.soru: Tap the numbers on the leaf section and see what each layer does.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.0.acik: The cuticle is a waterproof, waxy layer. It reduces water loss from the leaf.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.1.acik: The upper epidermis is a single row of clear cells. It lets light in and protects the tissues below.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.2.acik: The palisade mesophyll is made of tightly packed cells rich in chloroplasts. Most of the photosynthesis happens here.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.3.acik: The cells of the spongy mesophyll are loosely packed. The air spaces between them make gas exchange easier.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.4.acik: This is a leaf vein. The xylem on top brings water and minerals, and the phloem below carries away the sugar that is made.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.5.acik: The lower epidermis covers the underside of the leaf. In most plants, most of the stomata are here.
cards.1.etk.noktalar.6.acik: A stoma is the opening between two guard cells. CO<sub>2</sub> enters here, and O<sub>2</sub> and water vapor leave.
cards.1.once.soru: In which layer of a leaf does most of the photosynthesis happen?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: The palisade mesophyll has tightly packed cells rich in chloroplasts.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: Epidermal cells usually have no chloroplasts.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: The cuticle is not a layer of cells. It is a waxy covering.
cards.2.p: A tissue made of cells that can divide is called a meristem. The apical meristem makes the plant grow taller. The cambium makes the stem thicker by producing xylem toward the inside and phloem toward the outside. In seasonal climates, one annual ring forms each year.
cards.2.key: Most monocots, such as wheat and corn, have no cambium, so no annual rings form.
cards.3.p: Dermal tissue is made of epidermis or cork. Parenchyma cells are alive and thin-walled. They carry out photosynthesis or store food. Among the supporting tissues, collenchyma is alive and flexible, while sclerenchyma is hard and dead.
cards.3.key: The bark of old stems is cork tissue made of dead cells. Flax and hemp fibers are sclerenchyma.
cards.3.once.soru: Which tissue makes a walnut shell hard?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: Sclerenchyma is made of cells that are hardened with lignin and mostly dead.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: Parenchyma cells are alive and thin-walled.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: Collenchyma is a living, flexible tissue. It is not hard.
cards.4.p: Xylem carries water and minerals from the root to the leaves. Its conducting cells are dead when mature. Phloem carries organic substances. Its sieve tube cells are alive, and the flow can go in both directions.
cards.4.svg#14: together they form the vascular bundle
cards.4.key: Xylem cells are dead and carry water upward. Phloem cells are alive and can carry food in both directions.
cards.4.etk.soru: Does each feature belong to xylem or phloem?
cards.4.etk.ogeler.5.2: In phloem, food flows from source to sink. The sink can be in the root or at a growing tip.
cards.4.once.soru: Which tissue carries sugar from the leaf to the root?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: Phloem carries organic substances from source to sink.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: Xylem carries water and minerals upward.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: The epidermis is a protective tissue. It does not transport anything.
cards.5.p: The root loads minerals into the xylem by active transport. Water follows by osmosis, and root pressure builds up. On humid nights, water drips from the edges of leaves. This is called guttation. However, root pressure is not enough to lift water to the top of tall trees.
cards.5.key: In guttation, drops of liquid water form. In transpiration, water leaves as vapor, and dew forms when moisture in the air condenses.
cards.5.once.soru: What causes the water drops seen on the edges of some leaves in the morning?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: At night, when transpiration slows, root pressure pushes water out through the leaf edges. This is called guttation.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: In transpiration, water leaves as vapor and no drops form.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: The drops come from inside the leaf, out of pores along the edges.
cards.6.p: The evaporation of water through the stomata is called transpiration. During transpiration, water in the xylem is pulled upward. Water molecules cling both to each other (cohesion) and to the vessel walls (adhesion). This lets the column of water rise without breaking.
cards.6.key: The plant spends no ATP on this, because the Sun provides the energy. A plant loses most of the water it takes up through transpiration, and transpiration cools the leaf.
cards.7.p: A stoma is the opening between two guard cells. In light, K+ ions enter the guard cells, and water follows them. As the cells swell, the stoma opens. In the dark or during drought, the stoma closes.
cards.7.key: During drought, the hormone abscisic acid closes the stoma. When the stoma closes, water loss drops, but so does the intake of CO₂.
cards.8.p: In phloem, food flows from a source, such as a mature leaf, to a sink, such as a root, a fruit or a growing tip. At the source, sugar is loaded, water enters and pressure rises. At the sink, pressure drops. This is called the pressure flow model.
cards.8.key: Phloem can carry food in both directions. Where the source and the sink are decides the direction of flow.
cards.9.p: Hormones control growth in very small amounts. Auxin suppresses side buds. This is called apical dominance. Cytokinin stimulates cell division, and gibberellin stimulates elongation. Abscisic acid closes the stomata, and ethylene ripens fruit.
cards.9.key: Ethylene is a gas, so one rotting apple ripens the ones next to it too. Gibberellin triggers germination, while abscisic acid keeps the seed dormant.
cards.10.p: A plant growing in response to the direction of a stimulus is called a tropism. The stem grows toward light, and the root grows toward gravity and water. A nastic movement does not depend on the direction of the stimulus. A sensitive plant folding up when touched is an example.
cards.10.key: The kinds of tropism are phototropism, gravitropism, hydrotropism, chemotropism (pollen tube) and thigmotropism (climbing plants). A tropism happens through growth and is permanent. A nastic movement happens through turgor and reverses.
cards.11.p: Pollen reaching the stigma is called pollination. Of the two sperm that arrive through the pollen tube, one fertilizes the egg and forms the 2n zygote. The other joins the polar nuclei and forms the 3n endosperm. This is called double fertilization.
cards.11.key: Pollen forms in the anther. The egg is inside the ovule in the ovary.
cards.11.once.soru: A bee carries pollen from one flower and drops it on the stigma of another flower. What is this called?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: Carrying pollen to the stigma is called pollination. Fertilization happens later.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: Fertilization is the joining of sperm and egg, and it happens after the pollen tube grows.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Germination is when a seed starts to grow.
cards.12.p: After fertilization, the ovule becomes the seed, and the ovary becomes the fruit. A seed needs water, a suitable temperature and oxygen to germinate. Some seeds also need light.
cards.12.key: Once a seed takes up water, its enzymes start working and the stored food is used up by respiration. That is why a germinating seed loses dry mass until it starts photosynthesis.
cards.13.p:
• The apical meristem makes a plant grow taller, and the cambium makes it grow thicker.
• Xylem carries water upward, and phloem carries food in both directions.
• Water rises by transpiration pull and root pressure. Light and K+ open the stomata.
• Hormones control growth and tropisms.
• In double fertilization, the zygote is 2n and the endosperm is 3n.
quiz.0.q: The root cells of a plant have 2n = 14 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in this plant's endosperm cells?
quiz.0.e: The endosperm forms when one sperm (n = 7) joins two polar nuclei (7 + 7). That is why it carries 3n = 21 chromosomes.
quiz.1.q: Match each plant hormone with its main effect.
quiz.1.e: Auxin suppresses side buds, and cytokinin stimulates cell division. Gibberellin lengthens the stem and starts germination. Abscisic acid closes the stomata during drought. Ethylene, a gas, ripens fruit.
quiz.2.q: Match each plant movement with its name.
quiz.2.e: Turning toward light is phototropism, growing in response to gravity is gravitropism and winding around a support is thigmotropism. A sensitive plant folding up does not depend on the direction of the stimulus and happens through turgor. It is a nastic movement.
quiz.3.q: On the morning after a humid night, water drops appear only at the tips along a plant's leaf edges, and the drops contain minerals. What causes the drops?
quiz.3.o.2: Water vapor in the air condensing (dew)
quiz.3.o.3: Root pressure pushing water through water pores
quiz.3.e: This is called guttation. When transpiration is low, root pressure pushes mineral-rich water from the xylem out through the water pores along the leaf edge. Dew forms on every surface and contains no minerals.
quiz.3.y.0: In transpiration, water leaves as vapor, and transpiration slows in humid night air. The drops are caused by root pressure.
quiz.3.y.1: The water leaving the stomata is vapor. The drops that contain minerals are pushed out through water pores by root pressure.
quiz.3.y.2: Dew forms on the whole surface and contains no minerals. Drops seen only at the edge tips are guttation.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Pull water to the top, open a stoma, prune the tip and germinate a seed.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Every day, a tree carries hundreds of liters of water meters upward without any pump. Open the stomata and see what happens to the water in the xylem.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: In a tall tree, what is the main force that lifts water to the top?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Root pressure pushes water up a little, but it is not enough on its own for tall trees.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: There are no water pumps in xylem. The plant spends no ATP moving water.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Water evaporating from the stomata pulls the column of water in the xylem upward. Root pressure only helps.
A:adimlar.1.metin: At night and during drought, the stoma is closed. Change the conditions and open the stoma.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: Light and water were both provided. K⁺ ions entered the guard cells, water followed them and the stoma opened.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Phloem carries the sugar made in the leaves from a source to a sink, where the sugar is used or stored. First look at a plant in summer and play it.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Now the same plant is in spring. The leaves have not opened yet, but the buds need sugar to grow.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: In spring, which way does sugar flow in the phloem?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: From the leaves to the root
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In spring, there are no mature leaves yet to carry out photosynthesis.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.yazi: From the root's store to the buds
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: In spring, the store in the root becomes the source, and sugar is carried up to the growing buds (the sink). Phloem is made of living cells and can carry food in both directions. Xylem is dead and carries water only upward.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A growing bud needs sugar. The food has to come from somewhere.
A:adimlar.4.metin: The cambium adds one ring to the stem each year. Grow this tree to 5 years old.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: 5 rings show that the tree is 5 years old. The rings are made of xylem, which is wood. The phloem stays thin and is pushed outward.
A:adimlar.5.metin: A gardener cuts off the top bud of the stem. Make a guess before you play.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: What happens when the tip is pruned?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The tip that made the plant grow taller was cut off.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Pruning does not kill the plant. Gardeners do it every year.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The suppression by auxin is lifted, and cytokinin from the root stimulates the side buds. So the plant branches out.
A:adimlar.6.metin: A seedling on a windowsill bends toward the light. This is called phototropism. The hormone auxin controls this bending. Make a guess before you play.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: On which side of the seedling does auxin collect?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: If it did, the lit side would grow longer and the seedling would bend away from the light.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Auxin moves to the shaded side and makes the cells there grow longer. As the shaded side lengthens, the tip of the seedling bends toward the light.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: It goes down to the root
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The bending depends on how the auxin moving down from the tip is split between the two sides.
A:adimlar.7.metin: A seed can wait dry for years. Provide the conditions it needs to germinate.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.tamam: Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature were enough. Once a seed takes up water, its enzymes work and the stored food is used up by respiration. Respiration also needs oxygen. Most seeds do not need light, but some do. The seed loses dry mass until it opens leaves and starts photosynthesis.
A:kapanis.0: Water rises because of transpiration pull in the leaves. Cohesion and adhesion keep the column of water from breaking. Root pressure helps.
A:kapanis.1: In light, K⁺ ions and water enter the guard cells and the stoma opens. During drought, abscisic acid closes the stoma.
A:kapanis.2: Xylem cells are dead and carry water upward. Phloem cells are alive and can carry sugar from source to sink in both directions.
A:kapanis.3: The cambium makes the stem thicker, and one ring forms each year. Auxin controls apical dominance and turning toward light.
A:kapanis.4: A seed needs water, oxygen and a suitable temperature to germinate.
